newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- soft, futures underperform.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- soft, futures underperform.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were slightly lower in early Monday action, as the futures contract underperformed cash.
As a few bid-wanted lists circulated, traders pegged cash prices about two to three basis points lower, but the futures contract was off more sharply.
September muni futures lost 16/32 to 117-27/32, while while September Treasury bond futures fell 5/32 to 112-12/32. The MOB spread narrowed to 175 ticks from 186 at the close on Thursday.
The softer tone to start the week mirrored a lower Treasury market, where the long bond was off 3/32 at 99-13/32 to yield 6.67 percent.
The focus for the week is on new deals and data.
Muni sales are expected to total $7 billion in 130 sales, the largest total this year, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

Negotiated offerings total $5.7 billion in 60 sales, with a $2.7 billion New Jersey Economic Development Authority taxable deal through Merrill Lynch & Co. topping the list. Merrill is expected to begin a retail order period on the issue on Monday.
The state said late Friday it had secured bids from insurers for the entire deal.

On the competitive side, 70 sales totaling $1.3 billion are scheduled for the week. A $300 million Massachusettes deal on Tuesday is the largest. Monday's largest deal is a $14 million issue from Burlington, Vt.
The market this week will also get several key economic reports, including durable goods for May on Wednesday, and the First Quarter Gross Domestic Product data on Friday.
In the secondary market, bids on Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority's FGIC 5.0s of 2023 were two basis points higher at 5.51 percent.
Michigan Municipal Bond Authority 5-1/8s of 2020 were up one basis point to 5.52 percent.
